evidence.curator_note: Equation 8.104 is the DISTONIC counterpart of 8.103 and is drawn accordingly: 'R' is joined by a horizontal bond to 'Y', Y carries a bare '+' (no dot) and sits at the top-left of the U-shaped chain, and the far (top-right) end of the chain carries a lone radical dot on carbon. The arrow is labelled 'rd' and the products are 'R. + [ring, with + over the Y that now sits in the ring]' - i.e. the carbon radical attacks the charged heteroatom and displaces R.. So the bond that breaks is Y-R and the bond that forms is Y-C(radical); the charge stays on Y throughout. ARC COUNT (convention D): Book draws 2 arc(s), both single-barbed fishhooks whose barbs converge downwards into the gap between Y and the radical carbon - onto the forming Y-C bond. Arc 1 has its tail on the R-Y bond; arc 2 has its tail at the radical dot on the far carbon. Moves <1,2> are those two drawn arcs (move 1 = the carbon odd electron, move 2 = one electron of the breaking Y-R bond); move <3> is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page) - it puts the second electron of the breaking Y-R bond on R, producing the R. the book prints. INSTANTIATION (convention F): the page prints no m/z and no intensity. This record uses Y = NH2 and R = CH3, i.e. the distonic ion CH3-N(+)H2-CH2CH2CH2-CH2., an isomer (H already transferred from C to N) of the N-methylbutylamine molecular ion, m/z 87.1037; the displacement closes the six-electron-stable five-membered ring to give the pyrrolidinium ion C4H10N+ (m/z 72.0802) with loss of CH3. (15.0235). Y = NH2 was chosen because p. 214 names NH2 as the group whose rd cyclisations are favourable, but the choice is the curator's, not the book's. LOCALIZATION (convention B): the SMILES puts the charge on nitrogen as a four-coordinate closed-shell ammonium ([NH2+:2] with two heavy neighbours and two H) and the odd electron on the terminal carbon ([CH2:6] with one bond = one unpaired electron in RDKit), exactly where the book draws '+' and '.', so both drawn arcs have real origins.

NO MØD rule is cross-linked; rule_index.json has no '8.104' key (chapter-8 index runs 8.1-8.14 only). Candidates were CHECKED, not assumed. (i) hTransition_saturated_1_alpha (IMS_bookCover.py), DFS '[C.]1[C]2[C]3[C]4[_A+]5([H]6)>>[C]1[C]2[C]3[C]4{-}1.[_A+.]5([H]6)', has the same LEFT-hand situation - a carbon radical at one end of a chain and an even-electron onium at the other - and its pattern really does match this record's precursor (RDKit test '[#6&v3]-[#6]-[#6]-[#6]-[N+;H1,H2,H3]' -> exactly one hit, atom maps (6,5,4,3,2)). But its RIGHT-hand side does the opposite of Equation 8.104: it closes a CARBON-carbon ring ({-}1 bonds C4 to C1) and EXPELS the charge site as the radical cation [_A+.], i.e. applied here it would give cyclobutane + CH3NH2+., whereas 8.104 closes the C-N ring and expels the alkyl radical. Wrong bond formed, wrong fragment expelled - listed in rule_mismatches. (ii) IMS_4_42_rd ('[C]1[C]2[C]3[C]4[C]5[Cl+.]6>>...') is the correct rd geometry but is chlorine-specific and needs an ODD-electron halogen charge site; RDKit test of '[#6]-[#6]-[#6]-[#6]-[#6]-[Cl+]' against this precursor returns 0 matches. (iii) The generic 'substituion' rule ('[_A]1[C]2[C]3[_A+.]4>>[_A.]1.[C]2[C]3[_A+]4{-}2') fails twice over: its charge site is written '[_A+.]', an odd-electron heteroatom, while 8.104's Y+ is an even-electron onium with the radical on carbon, and all its '_A' placeholders unify to the same element, so the expelled group would have to be a heteroatom of the same element as Y rather than the alkyl R. drawn. No rule in the set encodes a distonic radical-site displacement.

NO MEASUREMENT ON THE PAGE (convention F): Equation 8.104 is drawn generically in R and Y and page 213 prints no m/z and no abundance for it. m/z 72.0802 (C4H10N+, pyrrolidinium) is curator-computed with RDKit ExactMolWt, electron-mass corrected, for the chosen instantiation Y = NH2, R = CH3 (precursor m/z 87.1037, expelled CH3. 15.0235). Status is therefore 'inferred', detected=false and relative_intensity is omitted.
